hubOrigin.headline: Foreign Drug Giants Undercut by Up to 95% in China Bidding

economicInterpretation: The event is not generically bullish for pharmaceuticals: centralized procurement compresses unit prices while reallocating volume and market share.
The investable question is which listed manufacturer can survive the price reset through low cost, multiple winning products, API integration or operational scale.
A diversified distributor with small winning-product exposure may receive little earnings benefit even if it wins many tenders.

candidates.name: 华海药业

evidence.claim: All three HuaHai products that entered the third centralized procurement round won bids: valsartan, olanzapine ODT and sertraline.
H1 revenue +24.6% YoY, attributable profit +72.8%, ex-item profit +102.9%, operating cash flow positive.

candidates.reasoning: Multiple wins plus already-improving earnings make the volume-share reallocation mechanism company-level rather than thematic. The API/formulation combination is potentially useful under severe price compression.

candidates.name: 华润双鹤

evidence.claim: Several subsidiaries/products were proposed winners in the third procurement round.
H1 revenue -14.8% YoY and attributable profit -13.2%, so the pre-existing earnings engine was weaker than HuaHai.

candidates.reasoning: Tender wins are real, but contemporaneous company earnings were contracting. This should not outrank a company with both share-gain evidence and operating acceleration.

candidates.name: 上海医药

evidence.source: National Business Daily / company disclosure summary
evidence.claim: Six products were proposed winners, but the listed company is highly diversified.
The group's scale is very large relative to the procurement-winning product set, weakening the earnings sensitivity of this single event.

candidates.reasoning: A high count of winning products does not automatically create high earnings sensitivity; expression purity is materially lower.

guardrails: Do not treat tender winning as positive unless post-cut price economics remain viable.
Do not equate number of products with earnings impact.
Final selection requires contemporaneous price/expectation and product-margin evidence.
